message.content:
**Decision: Buy.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and the fundamentals support a modest addition to the account.

**What the 10-K showed:** Total net sales of $391.0B (+2% YoY) with Services growing 13% to $96.2B — now 25% of revenue at a 73.9% gross margin, versus 37.2% for hardware — which lifted total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%. Operating income rose to $123.2B from $114.3B, and operating cash flow was a very strong $118.3B. Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) solely because of a one-time, non-cash-ish $10.2B net tax charge from the EC State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%) — the underlying operating trend is still improving. The balance sheet carries $140.8B in cash and marketable securities, $97.3B of term debt, and the company returned ~$110B to shareholders ($95B of buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends). Watch items that argue for a measured position rather than a large one: Greater China net sales fell 8% to $67.0B, iPad and Wearables declined, and legal/regulatory risk is meaningful (DOJ smartphone antitrust suit, DMA non-compliance proceedings in the EU with fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales).

**What I did:** With AAPL trading at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed one limit buy for 44 shares at $223.00 — roughly 0.13% above the market, well within "close to market" — which filled at $223.00 for about $9,812. That stays under the $10,000 per-order cap, leaves the $20,000 daily limit and the $50,000 cash balance untouched, and keeps me in only AAPL and MSFT with no withdrawals. Key figures relied on: FY2024 revenue $391.035B, operating income $123.216B, net income $93.736B, diluted EPS $6.08, operating cash flow $118.254B.
message.reasoning: Order filled at 223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Within $10k and within $20k daily cap. Summary.
